why_now: Channel: submitted as ANY → DEV. It is a devotional song idea; it fits no other channel.

Huge Short-form demand right now: our collector saw 'Respect zone 111+' Shorts titled 'He Shri Sheesh Ke Daani' at 1.73M views ~10h after upload (published 25 Sep), 1.36M and 1.19M on two more from 24 Sep (all 13–20 sec edits).
Other small channels are also getting 150–230K views in hours on 'Sheesh ke Daani' Shorts (khatu shayam manona dham, 25 Sep). The phrase 'Sheesh ke Daani' is the hook of the moment.
YouTube autocomplete today: 'khatu shyam bhajan' → 'new', 'new 2025', 'mandir', 'remix', 'song' — people search for NEW bhajans, so an original has room.

Key dates (verified): Shyam Janmotsav = Kartik Shukla Ekadashi (Dev Uthani) = Fri 20 Nov 2026 → T-14 brief 6 Nov, publish window 13–19 Nov, T-5 hard deadline 15 Nov. Next Gyaras (Papankusha Ekadashi) = 21/22 Oct (sources differ by a day — check local panchang). Phalgun Lakhi Mela starts 9 Mar 2027.
Evergreen: Khatu Shyam devotees listen every Gyaras (Shukla Ekadashi) and at the Phalgun Mela, so the video keeps earning after Janmotsav.

Gap vs competitors: viral Shorts are 13–20 sec clips of existing songs stuffed with unrelated hashtags — no lyrics, no story, no original music. Long-form is mostly live-kirtan re-uploads (e.g. TORANDWAR BHAKTI, 1–19K views each). Nobody pairs an original, clean-audio bhajan with on-screen lyrics and the 60-second Sheesh Daan story.

risk_flags: COPYRIGHT: almost every popular Khatu Shyam bhajan (Kanhaiya Mittal, Saawariya, Sonotek, T-Series etc.) is label-owned — do NOT cover or remix them, and do not reuse the audio in the viral 'Sheesh ke Daani' Shorts. Only an ORIGINAL composition passes. The common 'Om Jai Shri Shyam Hare' aarti carries named authors in its last stanza and is sung in versions attributed to 20th-century devotees, so its public-domain status is unclear — leave it out (or treat as Needs check) until rights are confirmed. Use original or licensed art; don't lift temple/shringar photos from other channels. Present the Barbarika story as 'according to tradition'; no miracle/wish-fulfilment promises in title or thumbnail (e.g. no 'sunte hi kaam banega'). Papankusha Ekadashi date differs by a day across sources (21 vs 22 Oct) — confirm with local panchang. No ledger overlap (no earlier Khatu Shyam card).
